newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - FTSE to edge up to 4,310 after weak start.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - FTSE to edge up to 4,310 after weak start.

text.p: After a weak start on Friday which may take the FTSE 100 index to around 4,290, the index should be able to edge a little higher to about 4,310, technical analysts said.

A straight head-to-head with its 25 day moving average has proved to be too much of a challenge for the market but while time is eroding that average, the index has remained steadfast and by this action alone it will go above it to indicate short-term strength, they added.
By 0725 GMT, at the pre-market open, the FTSE was indicated down 5.7 at 4,293.2.
Buying pressure has dropped recently and although it is not quite on the brink of collapse, the market will not find it easy to accelerate upwards today, analysts said.
Most at risk will be financial and pharmaceutical stocks, but these may pick up later in the day whereas some shares in the drinks sector should fare better, they added.
The market has been less than happy to go above 4,300 and has closed below it over the past two days casting doubt on the chances for any major strenghthening.
But it has been less volatile -- confining its daily average movement within a 25 point range so far this week.

Total market turnover has also declined slightly this week as the FTSE began to flatten out. And coupled with its slow pace, the market looks vulnerable to some downside pressure especially if Wall Street falls, analysts said.
But the Dow looks to be on its way to making a normal 50 percent retracement from its intra-day low of 6,356 on April 14 after its peak at 7,112 on March 11.
That would take the Dow to 6,734 near-term, and such a move should help lift the FTSE next week, analysts added.
On Thursday, the Dow closed down 21.27 at 6,658.60.
